title: Convert standard two-injective Hom models to native row-sign models
statement: Fix the finite field, prime and scheme hypotheses of [def-sf-native-weil-closed-models]. For any standard two-injective native Hom model $m$ supplied by [lem-sf-ringed-forget-two-injective-hom], there exist native row-sign Hom models $M$ with the same native and underlying derived Hom bifunctors as $m$, and a derived comparison $\eta$ equal to $m$'s derived comparison. Its NativeHomRepresentativeCompatibility square holds for the row-sign representatives: on every product projection the chain comparison is forgetting the native projection, and the localized square includes the canonical mapDerivedCategoryFactors. This only converts representative conventions; it does not assert any tensor structure, evaluation compatibility, or biduality.

source.place: Internal-Hom comparison, naturality of evaluation, and transposition paragraph; native refinement of lem-sf-weil-native-closed-forgetful.

proof.text: For each StandardModel construct the degreewise inverse product maps multiplying projection p in degree n by (n*p).negOnePow. Joint monicity of the product projections proves the two inverse identities. Its standard differential formula and the native row formula give a chain isomorphism; (n+1)*p=n*p+p and n*(p+1)=n*p+n give the two signs. The map_projection field proves simultaneous naturality. These are the private rowDegreeIso, rowIso and rowIso_naturality constructions.

Compose each supplied representative isomorphism with Q of this sign isomorphism. The supplied naturality and rowIso_naturality prove NativeHomRepresentatives. To identify the ordinary source slice with bifunctorRHom, restrict to the full homotopy category of K-injectives: use the target kInjectiveRepIso, the representative model, and quotientCompQhIso. Every homotopy arrow has a chain representative, so representative naturality and quotientCompQhIso naturality give a natural isomorphism there. Transport along the equivalence HomotopyCategory.KInjectives.Qh. This gives the private sliceModel, without a new existence assumption.

Keep m.hom, m.underlyingHom and m.native; use the preceding row representatives and sliceModel to construct rowClosedModel explicitly. Keep the comparison m.derived. For every two-K-injective pair conjugate m.chain by the inverse source sign map and the target sign map. The two signs cancel on each projection because forgetting is additive and the native sheaf-Hom comparison is the identity on underlying maps. Preservation of K-injectives is forgetKInjective. For the localized square use the supplied derived_representative square and naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors with the source sign isomorphism; its image cancels the inverse source sign. This is rowCompatibility.

Use rowClosedModel and the supplied m.derived as the existential witnesses. The two functor equalities and the comparison equality are HEq.rfl; rowCompatibility is the remaining conjunct. No uniqueness of an arbitrarily normalized comparison is used.

proof_origin.place: Internal-Hom comparison paragraph; explicit standard-to-row sign conjugation and localization naturality, formalized by D2.

from.place: The ancestor command returns None for the native obligation. This is the stated native refinement of the internal-Hom/evaluation/transposition paragraph in cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance.

lean.statement: theorem native_row_hom_comparison (m : TwoInjectiveHomModel (k₀ := k₀) (l := l) (X := X)) : ∃ M : NativeClosedHomModels k₀ l X, ∃ η : M.weilHom ⋙ nativeForget k₀ l X ≅ (nativeForget k₀ l X).op.prod (nativeForget k₀ l X) ⋙ M.ordinaryHom, HEq M.weilHom m.hom ∧ HEq M.ordinaryHom m.underlyingHom ∧ HEq η m.derived ∧ NativeHomRepresentativeCompatibility (ihomBifunctor k₀ l X) (ordinaryIhomBifunctor l (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).geometricFiber) M.weilHom M.ordinaryHom M.weilRepresentatives M.ordinaryRepresentatives (Endofunctor.IsoAlgebra.forget (WeilSheaf.frobeniusPullback k₀ l X)) η
